What may happen: Define purpose, invariants, initial harms, user vocabulary, and research questions.
What may not happen: No prototype, no user data, no user study, no deployment claim.
Promotion evidence: Completed concept contract and initial stop conditions.

What may happen: Threat model, counsel question drafting, data map, accessibility plan, protocol design, synthetic test plan.
What may not happen: No interactive prototype with real user data or production access.
Promotion evidence: Approved research protocol and defined evidence requirements.

What may happen: Local prototype, synthetic accounts, fictional data, static UI, unit/integration/security/accessibility tests.
What may not happen: No real-user content, no public release, no live matching/discovery.
Promotion evidence: Gate evidence from synthetic tests and unresolved-risk register.

What may happen: Limited research with explicit study consent, accessible withdrawal, no production decision impact, minimal data.
What may not happen: No hidden experiment, no undisclosed enrollment, no feature expansion, no reuse of data outside protocol.
Promotion evidence: Study protocol, human-review plan, privacy boundaries, stop conditions, participant-access plan.

What may happen: Narrow feature availability for a clearly defined, consenting audience under strong monitoring and immediate withdrawal.
What may not happen: No broad rollout, no paid promotion, no silent ranking, no unreviewed data expansion.
Promotion evidence: Passed critical gates, reviewed limitations, remediation path, appeal route.

What may happen: Feature available within reviewed technical and policy boundaries.
What may not happen: No use beyond documented scope, no hidden changes, no lapsed legal/security/accessibility review.
Promotion evidence: Current evidence, release approval, monitoring limited to permitted aggregate measures.

What may happen: Documentation, synthetic analysis, and review preparation only.
What may not happen: No real-user prototype or production availability.
Promotion evidence: Qualified counsel, security, privacy, or accessibility review as applicable.

What may happen: Re-scope object under a new version.
What may not happen: No advancement of the current design version.
Promotion evidence: New primary promise, revised model, fresh gates, renewed evidence plan.

What may not happen: No implementation, no hidden revival, no renamed reintroduction without a new independent proposal.
Promotion evidence: None; closure is final for that feature version.

What may happen: Preserve minimal governance record and implement safe removal.
What may not happen: No reactivation of the same version.
Promotion evidence: New version and entirely new review if research resumes.
